text:
{{Short description|48th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1978–79 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 15 October 1978 – 6 May 1979 |teams = |team1 = Tipperary |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 14th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two= Kerry |previous = [[1977–78 National Hurling League|1977–78]] |next = [[1979–80 National Hurling League|1979–80]] }} The '''1978–79 National Hurling League''' was the 48th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season | image=GAA-1979-National-Hurling-League-Final-Galway-Tipperary.jpg | image_size = 250 |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1978-79 |winners=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]
14th National League title
Captain: [[Paddy Williams]] |relegated=[[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1977-78 National Hurling League|1977-78]] |nextseason=[[1979-80 National Hurling League|1979-80]] |updated=1 March 2017 }} [[Clare GAA|Clare]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1977-78 National Hurling League|1977-78 season]]. [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 6 May 1979, [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] won the title after a 3–15 to 0–8 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final. It was their 14th league title overall and their first since [[1967-68 National Hurling League|1967-68]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/sporadic-rivalry-promises-to-fascinate-again-1.626596|title=Sporadic rivalry promises to fascinate again|publisher=Irish Times|date=24 July 2010|accessdate=28 February 2017|first=|last=}} Carlow were relegated from Division 1 after just one season in the top flight. ===Division 1A table=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: centre;" !width=20|Pos !width=150|Team !width=20|Pld !width=20|W !width=20|D !width=20|L !width=20|Pts !width=250|Notes |- |'''1'''||align=left|''' [[Clare GAA|Clare]] '''||'''6'''||'''5'''||'''1'''||'''0'''||'''11''' |- style="background:silver;" |'''2'''||align=left|''' [[Galway GAA|Galway]] '''||'''6'''||'''3'''||'''2'''||'''1'''||'''8'''|| Division 1 runners-up |- |'''3'''||align=left|''' [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] '''||'''6'''||'''3'''||'''1'''||'''2'''||'''7''' |- style |'''4'''||align=left|''' [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] '''||'''6'''||'''2'''||'''2'''||'''2'''||'''6''' |- |'''5'''||align=left|''' [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] '''||'''6'''||'''2'''||'''0'''||'''4'''||'''4''' |- style="background:#FFC0CB;" |'''6'''||align=left|''' [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] '''||'''6'''||'''2'''||'''0'''||'''4'''||'''4'''|| Relegated to Division 1B |- style="background:#FFC0CB;" |'''7'''||align=left|''' [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] '''||'''6'''||'''1'''||'''0'''||'''5'''||'''2'''|| Relegated to Division 1B |} ===Group stage=== {{football box collapsible | date = 1 October 1978 | team1 = [[Galway GAA|Galway]] | score = 3-12 -
